title: win32-x64 release qualification fails deterministically at the sacrificial native probe, and the refusal message discards the error it measured
description:
Measured 2026-09-30 on the v0.12.0 release build: run 36704337353, attempts 1 AND 2 both failure, only `matching-host package qualification (win32-x64)` red, step "Build, pack, install, smoke, uninstall, and audit win32-x64". The refusal reads `Windows native probe failed without a proven abrupt native stop (exit=1, signal=none, stdout=sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855, stderr=sha256:da81e8ef0e05ee7d07aeb831953aa5a8bcf7de02f93b1e2b20dce68776eff090)`.

MECHANISM, read from source rather than inferred from the message: benchmark/ladybug/native-probe.ts writes `native-import-started` before loadLadybugNativeDriver(), `native-import-completed` after it, and `native-import-failed` in its catch handler. isProvenAbruptWindowsImportCrash requires exit != 0 AND started AND NOT completed AND NOT failed. The observed shape -- exit=1, signal=none, empty stdout, non-empty stderr -- is the CATCH-HANDLER signature: a normal JavaScript rejection at the native driver load, not a native crash. So the child failed to LOAD the Ladybug driver on win32-x64, and the probe correctly refused to call that either a pass or a proven crash.

WHY IT IS RELEASE-ONLY, which is why no earlier gate caught it: every ladybug test is describe.skip on win32 (test/ladybug-lifecycle.test.ts:41-63, test/ladybug-concurrency.test.ts:81, test/workspace-retrieval.test.ts:29), the benchmark smoke job runs on ubuntu-24.04 only, and win32-arm64's pass in the same run is vacuous -- runNativeProbe returns probeMode "unavailable" when ladybugPackage === null, which is the Windows-ARM64 case, so that leg never loads the driver at all. win32-x64 is the ONLY Windows leg that loads it, and it only runs at release time.

THE ONE CHANGED VARIABLE, from `git diff v0.11.0 v0.12.0`: the qualification script now asserts Bun 1.4.2 (was 1.3.14) and package.json's engines/packageManager/@types/bun moved with it, lockfile included; @ladybugdb/core is 0.19.0 at both tags. The setup-bun cache key includes the lockfile hash, so the fresh install on this run is not a stale-cache artifact. The same 1.3.14 to 1.4.2 transition is what quest-cli isolated on their own Windows legs (QCLI-426), which is the first thing to compare against rather than bisecting first.

BLOCKED BY THIS: the failed leg skips `package + install-sanity (dry-run, never publishes)`, so the run produces no `npm-packages` artifact; opum-cli-e2e therefore cannot produce the matched quest 0.12.0 + lore 0.12.0 receipts, and those receipts gate quest's staging and the whole DEC-55 train.

DIAGNOSTIC GAP, owed independently of the cause and confirmed by the orchestrator: the refusal prints sha256 DIGESTS of the child's stdout and stderr and not the text, and not the three marker booleans -- so this failure cannot be diagnosed from the log, the jobs API, or the artifact (which holds only the two tarballs; the JSON report is written after the throw). Both pieces are already computed at the call site. A green re-run would otherwise have hidden this gap.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The Windows refusal message names the three import marker booleans and carries a bounded tail of the child's stderr, proven by a positive control that fails a deliberate rejection and shows both.
The actual error text of the win32-x64 Ladybug driver-load rejection under the bun 1.4.2 pin is quoted in this record's notes.
A qualification run whose artifacts are the ones opum-cli-e2e binds reports the win32-x64 leg green, with that run's id recorded here.

plan: 1. Add the three import-marker booleans and a bounded stderr tail to the Windows refusal message in benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts, with a unit test that drives a deliberate rejection and asserts both appear.
2. Run the diagnostics from a branch ref to capture the actual win32-x64 driver-load error text (release.yml dispatch on the branch, publish=false), and quote it on this record.

3. With the error text in hand, identify the cause under the bun 1.4.2 pin, land the fix (reviewer pass per CLAUDE.md), and re-run the qualification to a green win32-x64 leg whose artifacts opum-cli-e2e binds.
implementationNotes: Diagnostics implemented and pushed on fix/LCLI-657-probe-refusal-carries-markers-and-output (commit 0de15525): the Windows refusal now carries markers={started,completed,failed} and a bounded head+tail excerpt of the child stderr (limit 4000, elision marked with its byte count); the non-Windows indexing refusal carries the same excerpt; the digest is retained as the identity of the bytes. Positive control, run rather than asserted: deleting the markers fragment reddens the new test alone (14 pass/1 fail), and separately collapsing the excerpt to its head reddens the same test alone (14 pass/1 fail) -- both mutants reverted, 15 pass/0 fail after, lint at its 7-warning baseline and typecheck clean. Diagnostic run 36705622741 dispatched on the BRANCH ref to capture the real error text; opum-cli-e2e has been told by id that this run is never bindable. Next: quote the error text here, then fix the cause.

AC2 EVIDENCE — the actual error, captured from diagnostic run 36705622741 (branch ref fix/LCLI-657..., job 109855679599) once the diagnostics landed:

Error: LoadLibrary failed: A dynamic link library (DLL) initialization routine failed.
    at dlopen (unknown)
    at <anonymous> (D:\a\lore-cli\lore-cli\node_modules\.bun\@ladybugdb+core@0.19.0\node_modules\@ladybugdb\core\lbug_native.js:12:8)
    at <anonymous> (…\@ladybugdb\core\connection.js:3:7)
    at <anonymous> (…\@ladybugdb\core\index.js:3:7)

markers={started:true, completed:false, failed:true}, stdout empty, exit=1, signal=none.

THREE READINGS THAT MATTER FOR THE FIX.
1. Line 12 of that file is the PATCHED line. Confirmed against this checkout's installed copy — 12 lines, `module.exports = require("./lbugjs.node")` at 12, zero occurrences of process.dlopen — so lore's patchedDependencies patch IS applied inside bun's isolated store, and the failing call travels bun's MODULE LOADER, not a literal process.dlopen call.
2. The Windows error is ERROR_DLL_INIT_FAILED (1114): the addon's DllMain returned FALSE. That is a native-side refusal, deterministic, with identical bytes at both attempts and both tags.
3. The same addon bytes loaded CLEANLY at v0.11.0 under bun 1.3.14 (that run's win32-x64 leg is green and the probe only accepts a clean import as a pass), so the trigger is the runtime transition, not the artifact.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE ON RECORD, so the next reader does not re-derive it: quest-cli read process.dlopen at bun-v1.3.14 / v1.4.0 / v1.4.2 and found NO Windows-semantic change in it (their one new hard-refusal path is Linux-only; the embedded-.node extraction change applies to compiled binaries). They named the object to read next: the module loader was REWRITTEN Zig to Rust in 1.4.0 — src/jsc/NodeModuleModule.zig -> NodeModuleModule.rs, alongside a wholly new src/runtime/ tree carrying runtime/napi/* — and confirmed they have NOT read that rewrite. Their extracted trees are at /tmp/bun-diff on this machine.

ARTIFACT-LEVEL RESULT — the decisive measurement, from diagnostic run 36706817656 (branch ref diag/LCLI-657-dlopen-probe, the acceptance deliberately relaxed to let the run continue past the refusal):

matching-host package qualification (win32-x64) · SUCCESS, and every downstream step that the red run never reached:
  Assemble Ladybug acceptance evidence · success
  package + install-sanity (dry-run, never publishes) · success
  publish · skipped (publish=false by design)   verify this release's own provenance · skipped (publish-gated)

So the packed tarballs, the installed global launcher, the relocated standalone executable, the smoke, the uninstall and the audit all pass on win32-x64 under bun 1.4.2. The ALREADY-PUBLISHED-CLAIM is the same: the shipped artifact is not affected by what the interpreter-path probe cannot do.

WHY THAT IS CONSISTENT RATHER THAN SURPRISING — Windows is reference-fallback-only BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement:
- benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts:392-393 computes `embeddedNativeIndexVerified` as `input.os !== "win32" && ...` — false on Windows by definition, never measured.
- :397-399 THROWS if a Windows host creates a Ladybug cache database ("Windows reference fallback unexpectedly created a Ladybug cache database").
- :262 requires `embeddedNativeIndexVerified === (os !== "win32")` in the report validator.
- docs/reference/architecture.md:386 — "proves reference fallback on both Windows architectures"; docs/reference/tech-stack.md:361 — "package qualifications therefore prove reference-fallback-only".
So the native addon's LOADABILITY is not a Windows product requirement, and never was. The failing probe is a characterization step — it accepts a clean import or a proven abrupt crash, both claiming reference-fallback-only — whose acceptance set has no arm for "the driver cannot load at all", which is exactly what bun 1.4.2 produces on this host.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE OPTIONS, recorded so the A/B rests on it: pinning the runtime back to 1.3.14 would unblock the train but reverses a breaking, test-backed contract change of this release (LCLI-648: 1.3.14 panics on a TS contextual-keyword shape; test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts fails on 1.3.14 and passes on 1.4.2). Holding for an upstream fix blocks quest's release too (opum-cli-e2e's pair lock refuses a mixed pair). Accepting the documented load failure on win32-x64 costs nothing user-visible, because the documented Windows support level is already reference-fallback-only.

CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS GREEN: it came from a branch whose Windows acceptance was deliberately relaxed for measurement. It is NOT a fix, it is NOT landable, and it must never be reported as a passing qualification of v0.12.0. The refusal stays in the real tree. Decision routed to opum-agent as an A/B packet for the operator.

REVIEW ROUNDS, recorded because they changed the change rather than only blessing it. Two adversarial passes over PR opum-ai/lore-cli#445, both accepted in full, head 9d1294e7.

PASS 1 findings and dispositions. F1+F2 (medium, the real ones): the first test asserted the refusal text in the runner's SOURCE, so it stayed green while the property was lost -- reproduced by parking the marker fragment in the sibling non-Windows refusal (whose three locals are also in scope) and by parking the excerpt in a comment. It was an identity check, not the control AC1 asked for. Fixed by making the refusal a VALUE driven with a deliberate rejection.
F3 (low): boundedNativeProbeOutput degenerate limits -- slice(-0) is slice(0), so limit 1 returned the whole string while claiming elision, and odd limits understated the drop by one. Fixed and pinned.
F4 (low): the head+tail rationale was inverted (a caught rejection is written message-first, stack deepest-frame-first, as this task's own captured stack shows) and the count was labelled bytes while measuring UTF-16 code units. Comment corrected.

PASS 2 findings and dispositions -- these are the ones that kept going. R1 (low-medium): the wiring assertion pinned the callee's NAME, and five mutants stayed green, including `stderr: ""` at the call site, which reproduces the LCLI-657 symptom exactly; a shadowed binding and a decoy in a comment also satisfied it. Fixed by extracting the guarded transition into a TOTAL classifier, classifyWindowsProbeOutcome, unit-tested over all three outcomes. The first form of that classifier handled only the two non-clean arms and therefore classified a clean import as a REFUSAL -- the new test caught it, which is the argument for the extraction having been right.
R2 (low): fractional, negative and NaN limits still degenerated like the old slice(-0) bug. Fixed by normalising before slicing.
R3 (low): the sibling non-Windows refusal had no control at all once the Windows assertions were scoped; deleting its excerpt reddened nothing. Fixed with its own builder and its own test.
R4 (informational): this note.

MUTATION PROOF for the final tests, each reddening ONLY its intended test with the others green: markers dropped from the composed message; excerpt dropped; throw inlined (no longer using the builder); swapped digest pair in the message; excerpt left unescaped (breaking the single-line property); sibling losing its excerpt (reddens the SIBLING test, the branch that had no coverage).

STALE CLAIM IN NOTE 1, superseded rather than rewritten: it says the elision is "marked with its byte count". The mark now counts UTF-16 code units, and the counts themselves were wrong for odd limits. History stays as written; this note is what corrects the forward reading.
